concepts.title: Tower Showroom
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity 16:9 landscape PC strategy GAME interface screenshot mock-up for Copilot Tower Defense, a friendly low-poly game. Modify the campus screenshot into the proposed interactive Tower inspection screen. Input image 1 is the campus setting/composition reference and edit target; input image 2 is the EXACT selected Developer model appearance; image 3 Security, image 4 Linter and image 5 Base are portrait/model references. Preserve those character identities: these are hovering heads without bodies, arms or legs. Developer has orange swept geometric spikes, chunky dark goggles with teal lenses, a dark face and two luminous cyan vertical eyes, cream hexagonal ear pods marked {}. Do not redesign it as a robot with a torso. The campus is an archipelago of connected flat hexagon tiles; its central small white 2-storey lab is the entrance to this menu. Product identity is "COPILOT HUB", never Glacier. Palette is desaturated deep navy, warm off-white, soft mint/aqua, small lilac highlights, matte bevelled game hardware. Restrained glow, playful premium strategy-game craftsmanship, legible crisp text and deliberate hierarchy. No website navigation, sidebar list, dashboard cards, tables, browser chrome, SaaS page, RPG health/mana/armor, monetization, fabricated power score, star ratings, or Deploy/Buy button. This is inspection, not purchasing. Show a genuine game roster of 7 compact portrait/selectors labelled "Base", "Developer", "Tester", "Analyst", "Security", "Architect", "Linter", with Developer clearly selected. Use references for known portraits, understated silhouette medallions for unavailable character art. A coherent rotatable 3D preview of the Developer with a curved orbit gesture and small "Drag to rotate · Scroll to zoom" hint; allow visible tilt affordance and a reset camera icon. Game animations strip labelled "Rest", "Idle", "Work", "Move", "Place", "Hit", "Resolve", with Idle active, a play/pause icon, a thin scrub timeline and "1×" speed. Stats are EXACT: "Damage 7 / action", "Work 5 / action", "Speed 2.5 / sec", "Range 5 units". Visualize stats as distinct restrained segmented gauges with precise numeric labels, and range as a faint radius ring around the model pedestal. Additional small cost badge "Persona +20 Compute" and tiny text "Base 30 · Total 50", making an upgrade not separate purchase explicit. Small badge "Playtest stats" because this is a design mockup. Name "DEVELOPER", role "Direct-output specialist". Persistent close/return action "Back to Hub". Keep compact text, no paragraphs, no tiny meaningless lorem ipsum. Polish all edges and typography.
DIRECTION A — TOWER SHOWROOM. This is a premium GAME loadout screen that opens over the dimmed actual campus. The campus is still recognizable along the outer margins and in soft focus; central building subtly outlined mint at the rear. A huge central-left live Developer hovering over a small cream hexagonal display plinth dominates 50% of the screen. Below the model a compact animation control rail, below that an elegant horizontal row of seven chunky portrait chips, like equipment sockets, NOT web cards. Right side a single bevelled vertically shaped dossier plate, asymmetrical clipped corners, masthead "TOWER SHOWROOM", the large name DEVELOPER, four short segmented stat gauges, cost badge. Generous uncluttered negative space. Top-left modest Copilot Hub branding and small tower emblem, top-right Back to Hub. One continuous composition, NOT a collage. Make the model itself richly lit and opaque, not transparent hologram. Background mint currents continue behind the UI. The end result should look directly shippable as a game inspection overlay, not an artwork advertising it.

DIRECTION B — LAB WORKBENCH. Distinct from a flat menu: the screen is an intimate isometric cutaway of the inside of the campus lab, a physical playable toy-like showroom with warm ivory walls, a wide window looking out onto the campus and its trees. A substantial cream inspection table occupies the center, with Developer hovering just above a circular mint-lit turntable, large and easily inspected. Stat gauges and labels belong to angled dark instrument panels integrated with the desk on the right; a curved ruler-shaped range gauge around the display. Along the front edge of the physical desk are seven small character portrait medallions set into brass/ivory sockets, like choosing a miniature. A compact floating animation transport strip just above the table lip. Very few additional props: only a small console and subtle architectural lighting, no people. Materials matte ivory, charcoal, teal, warm wood details. All UI remains straight/readable enough to operate. Title "TOWER LAB" etched into the top-left structural frame; Developer name/role in a neat hovering label. Back to Hub is a clear attached top-right control. This should feel like visiting an interactive game location, not a dashboard. No giant bright beams or sci-fi clutter. A cohesive finished 3D game interface.

DIRECTION C — TOWER CODEX. A tactical collectible-character GAME menu inspired by beautifully designed physical field manuals and chunky game cards. The main focus is ONE large cream dossier card with cut corners, not a grid of web cards, standing slightly raised over the blue digital campus surface. Developer occupies the left 60% of this card as an interactive 3D model emerging above a small hex pedestal, with generous visual space. The right 40% is a restrained dark navy inset of embossed icons, four stat meters and exact numbers. Orange edge tab matches Developer orange; tiny mint selection rune. Bottom of this single large card holds the slim animation strip. At far left, show a short fanned deck of smaller portrait cards for the other towers with prominent art and minimal labels, and a simple previous/next chevron; all seven roster options represented, selected Developer card elevated. The fanned deck is a visual game collection, no scrolling text sidebar. Header "TOWER CODEX" with Copilot Hub as a small breadcrumb. Campus geometry very subdued in the background, fine digital currents. Physical paper/ceramic-like surface contrasted with metallic hinges and clean mint indicators. Strong tactile depth, readable type, a calm colorful low-poly character, no excessive weathering, no fantasy scrollwork. Entire final interface fits in one 16:9 screen.
